topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes for the lecture on cancer causes.

topics.label: Origins, Risk Factors, and Epidemiology of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the basic biological nature of cancer and explore how endogenous cellular errors, environmental exposures, and population-level epidemiological variations shape overall cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how various infectious pathogens drive malignant transformation, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study of pathogen cooperation and chromosomal translocation.

topics.label: Chemical and Radiation Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how environmental chemicals, dietary toxins, and ultraviolet radiation undergo xenobiotic activation or direct reaction to form DNA adducts and mutagenic lesions.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, chronic inflammatory responses, and host developmental stages create permissive environments for malignant clonal expansion.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the experimental, genomic, epidemiological, and toxicological methodologies used to assess mutagenicity and prove causal links between exposures and cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing the main takeaways regarding environmental cancer risk and practical risk-benefit decisions in everyday life.
